name: unsafe fn as_inner (& mut self) -> & mut Self :: Source

name: trait TrustedRandomAccess : TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce
rule: Implementors of TrustedRandomAccess must ensure that the iterator's size_hint is exact.

name: trait TrustedRandomAccess : TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce
rule: Implementors of TrustedRandomAccess must ensure that the iterator's size_hint is cheap to call.

name: trait TrustedRandomAccess : TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce
rule: Implementors of TrustedRandomAccess must not override TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce::size.

name: trait TrustedRandomAccess : TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce
rule: All subtypes and all supertypes of a type implementing TrustedRandomAccess must also implement TrustedRandomAccess. In particular, implementations for types with non-invariant parameters usually cannot depend on trait bounds on those parameters, except bounds from the struct or enum definition itself or bounds involving traits with a similar subtype/supertype guarantee.

name: trait TrustedRandomAccess : TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce
rule: If Self implements ExactSizeIterator, implementors of TrustedRandomAccess must ensure that self.len() always produces results consistent with self.size().

name: trait TrustedRandomAccess : TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce
rule: If Self implements Iterator, <Self as Iterator>::__iterator_get_unchecked(&mut self, idx) must be safe to call provided all of these conditions hold: 0 <= idx < self.size(); if Self does not implement Clone, the same index is never requested on self more than once; after the unchecked access, next_back() is called at most self.size() - idx - 1 times, with this limit calculated separately for self and each clone but counting next_back() calls before cloning against both; after the unchecked access, only Clone::clone, Iterator::size_hint, DoubleEndedIterator::next_back, ExactSizeIterator::len, Iterator::__iterator_get_unchecked, and TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce::size are called on self or any new clones. Coercion from Self to any supertype T is permitted, including multiple successive coercions; after an unchecked access, the same method restriction applies to every resulting coerced value, and the same-index unchecked-access counts and next_back() counts are summed across self and successive coercion results and must remain within the stated bounds.

name: trait TrustedRandomAccess : TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce
rule: If Self implements Iterator, implementors of TrustedRandomAccess must ensure that __iterator_get_unchecked(&mut self, idx) does not change the value returned by size_hint, provided all of these conditions hold: 0 <= idx < self.size(); if Self does not implement Clone, the same index is never requested on self more than once; after the unchecked access, next_back() is called at most self.size() - idx - 1 times, with this limit calculated separately for self and each clone but counting next_back() calls before cloning against both; after the unchecked access, only Clone::clone, Iterator::size_hint, DoubleEndedIterator::next_back, ExactSizeIterator::len, Iterator::__iterator_get_unchecked, and TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce::size are called on self or any new clones. Coercion from Self to any supertype T is permitted, including multiple successive coercions; after an unchecked access, the same method restriction applies to every resulting coerced value, and the same-index unchecked-access counts and next_back() counts are summed across self and successive coercion results and must remain within the stated bounds.

name: trait TrustedRandomAccess : TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce
rule: If Self implements Iterator, implementors of TrustedRandomAccess must ensure that, after __iterator_get_unchecked(&mut self, idx), it remains safe to call Clone::clone, Iterator::size_hint, DoubleEndedIterator::next_back, ExactSizeIterator::len, Iterator::__iterator_get_unchecked, and TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce::size on self when the required traits are implemented, provided all of these conditions hold: 0 <= idx < self.size(); if Self does not implement Clone, the same index is never requested on self more than once; after the unchecked access, next_back() is called at most self.size() - idx - 1 times, with this limit calculated separately for self and each clone but counting next_back() calls before cloning against both; after the unchecked access, only those listed methods are called on self or any new clones. Coercion from Self to any supertype T is permitted, including multiple successive coercions; after an unchecked access, the same method restriction applies to every resulting coerced value, and the same-index unchecked-access counts and next_back() counts are summed across self and successive coercion results and must remain within the stated bounds.

name: trait TrustedRandomAccess : TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce
rule: If Self implements Iterator, implementors of TrustedRandomAccess must ensure that it is safe to drop self after __iterator_get_unchecked(&mut self, idx), provided all of these conditions hold: 0 <= idx < self.size(); if Self does not implement Clone, the same index is never requested on self more than once; after the unchecked access, next_back() is called at most self.size() - idx - 1 times, with this limit calculated separately for self and each clone but counting next_back() calls before cloning against both; after the unchecked access, only Clone::clone, Iterator::size_hint, DoubleEndedIterator::next_back, ExactSizeIterator::len, Iterator::__iterator_get_unchecked, and TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce::size are called on self or any new clones. Coercion from Self to any supertype T is permitted, including multiple successive coercions; after an unchecked access, the same method restriction applies to every resulting coerced value, and the same-index unchecked-access counts and next_back() counts are summed across self and successive coercion results and must remain within the stated bounds.

name: trait TrustedRandomAccess : TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce
rule: If Self implements Iterator and is a subtype of T, implementors of TrustedRandomAccess must ensure that it is safe to coerce self to T after __iterator_get_unchecked(&mut self, idx), provided all of these conditions hold: 0 <= idx < self.size(); if Self does not implement Clone, the same index is never requested on self more than once; after the unchecked access, next_back() is called at most self.size() - idx - 1 times, with this limit calculated separately for self and each clone but counting next_back() calls before cloning against both; after the unchecked access, only Clone::clone, Iterator::size_hint, DoubleEndedIterator::next_back, ExactSizeIterator::len, Iterator::__iterator_get_unchecked, and TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce::size are called on self or any new clones. Multiple successive coercions to supertypes are permitted; after an unchecked access, the same method restriction applies to every resulting coerced value, and the same-index unchecked-access counts and next_back() counts are summed across self and successive coercion results and must remain within the stated bounds.

name: trait TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce : Sized
rule: After `__iterator_get_unchecked` is called on an iterator implementing `TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce`, the iterator must not be coerced to a supertype.

name: trait TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce : Sized
rule: For safety, subtypes and supertypes of a type implementing `TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce` need not implement `TrustedRandomAccessNoCoerce`.

name: unsafe fn forward_unchecked (start : Self , count : usize) -> Self
rule: Calling `Step::forward_unchecked(start, count)` must not overflow the range of values supported by `Self` when taking the successor of `start` `count` times; such overflow is undefined behavior.

name: unsafe fn forward_unchecked (start : Self , count : usize) -> Self
rule: If there exists a value `b` such that `b > start`, it is safe to call `Step::forward_unchecked(start, 1)`.

name: unsafe fn forward_unchecked (start : Self , count : usize) -> Self
rule: If there exist a value `b` and a count `n` such that `Step::steps_between(&start, &b) == Some(n)`, it is safe to call `Step::forward_unchecked(start, count)` for any `count <= n`.

name: unsafe fn forward_unchecked (start : Self , count : usize) -> Self
rule: Calling `Step::forward_unchecked(start, 0)` is always safe.

name: unsafe fn backward_unchecked (start : Self , count : usize) -> Self
rule: For safety, taking the predecessor of `start` `count` times in `Step::backward_unchecked(start, count)` must not overflow the range of values supported by `Self`.

name: unsafe fn backward_unchecked (start : Self , count : usize) -> Self
rule: If there exists `b` such that `b < start`, it is safe to call `Step::backward_unchecked(start, 1)`.

name: unsafe fn backward_unchecked (start : Self , count : usize) -> Self
rule: If there exist `b` and `n` such that `Step::steps_between(&b, &start) == (n, Some(n))`, it is safe to call `Step::backward_unchecked(start, count)` for any `count <= n`.

name: unsafe fn backward_unchecked (start : Self , count : usize) -> Self
rule: It is always safe to call `Step::backward_unchecked(start, 0)`.

name: unsafe fn extend_one_unchecked (& mut self , item : A) where Self : Sized ,
rule: Callers of `extend_one_unchecked` must ensure that the collection has enough capacity to contain the new item.

name: unsafe fn extend_one_unchecked (& mut self , item : A) where Self : Sized ,
rule: An implementation of `extend_one_unchecked` may rely on the capacity precondition for safety, including allowing undefined behavior if it is violated, only if the collection implements `extend_reserve` correctly.

name: unsafe fn extend_one_unchecked (& mut self , item : A) where Self : Sized ,
rule: Callers that have reserved enough space with `extend_reserve` may safely call `extend_one_unchecked` to add an item within that reserved capacity.

name: trait TrustedFused
rule: Implementations of TrustedFused must not be lifetime-dependent.

name: trait TrustedLen : Iterator
rule: Implementors of TrustedLen must ensure that Iterator::size_hint() either has equal lower and upper bounds or has an upper bound of None.

name: trait TrustedLen : Iterator
rule: Implementors of TrustedLen must ensure that Iterator::size_hint() has an upper bound of None only if the actual iterator length is greater than usize::MAX.

name: trait TrustedLen : Iterator
rule: If Iterator::size_hint() has an upper bound of None, implementors of TrustedLen must ensure that its lower bound is usize::MAX, yielding (usize::MAX, None).

name: trait TrustedLen : Iterator
rule: Implementors of TrustedLen must ensure that the iterator produces exactly the number of elements it reported or diverges before reaching the end.

name: trait TrustedLen : Iterator
rule: Consumers of TrustedLen must inspect the upper bound returned by Iterator::size_hint().

name: trait InPlaceIterable
rule: Implementors must guarantee that each step of any method that advances the iterator, such as next() or try_fold(), has moved out at least one value from the iterator's underlying SourceIter.

name: trait InPlaceIterable
rule: Implementors must guarantee that, for each step of any method that advances the iterator, the iterator chain's result could be inserted in place of a moved-out underlying source value, assuming the source's structural constraints allow such an insertion.

name: trait TrustedStep : Step + Copy
rule: Consumers of TrustedStep may rely on all invariants of every method of the type's Step implementation in unsafe code.

name: trait Send
rule: Implementing `Send` for a type requires that values of that type can be safely transferred across thread boundaries.

name: trait Sync
rule: A type `T` may implement `Sync` if and only if passing shared references `&T` between threads cannot cause undefined behavior, including data races; equivalently, `&T` must be `Send`.

name: trait Sync
rule: Shared references to `&T` and `&mut T` may safely be passed between threads if and only if `T` is `Sync`.

name: trait Sync
rule: Any type with interior mutability must wrap values that can be mutated through a shared reference in `cell::UnsafeCell`; failing to do so is undefined behavior.

name: trait Sync
rule: Transmuting a shared reference `&T` into a mutable reference `&mut T` is invalid.

name: trait Freeze
rule: Implementors must not implement `Freeze` for other types.

name: unsafe fn take (slot : & mut ManuallyDrop < T >) -> T
rule: After calling `ManuallyDrop::take(slot)`, the caller must ensure that the `ManuallyDrop<T>` container in `slot` is not used again.

name: unsafe fn take (slot : & mut ManuallyDrop < T >) -> T
rule: The pointer to the contained value in `slot` must be valid for reads.

name: unsafe fn take (slot : & mut ManuallyDrop < T >) -> T
rule: The pointer to the contained value in `slot` must be properly aligned for `T`, even if `T` has size 0.

name: unsafe fn take (slot : & mut ManuallyDrop < T >) -> T
rule: The contained value in `slot` must be a properly initialized value of type `T`.

name: unsafe fn drop (slot : & mut ManuallyDrop < T >)
rule: The pointer to the value contained in `slot` must be valid for both reads and writes when `ManuallyDrop::drop(slot)` is called.

name: unsafe fn drop (slot : & mut ManuallyDrop < T >)
rule: The pointer to the value contained in `slot` must be properly aligned, even if `T` has size zero.

name: unsafe fn drop (slot : & mut ManuallyDrop < T >)
rule: The pointer to the value contained in `slot` must be nonnull, even if `T` has size zero.

name: unsafe fn drop (slot : & mut ManuallyDrop < T >)
rule: The value contained in `slot` must be valid for dropping, including any type-specific invariants required by its destructor.

name: unsafe fn drop (slot : & mut ManuallyDrop < T >)
rule: While `ManuallyDrop::drop(slot)` is executing, parts of the contained value may be accessed only through the `&mut self` references supplied to the `Drop::drop` methods it invokes.

name: unsafe fn drop (slot : & mut ManuallyDrop < T >)
rule: After `ManuallyDrop::drop(slot)`, the dropped "zombie" value must not be exposed to safe code.

name: unsafe fn drop (slot : & mut ManuallyDrop < T >)
rule: `ManuallyDrop::drop(slot)` must not be called more than once on the same contained value.

name: unsafe fn drop (slot : & mut ManuallyDrop < T >)
rule: If `T` is not `Copy`, using the contained value after `ManuallyDrop::drop(slot)` can cause undefined behavior; assigning a new value over it counts as a use because that drops the old value again.

name: unsafe fn drop (slot : & mut ManuallyDrop < T >)
rule: Except for changes made by the destructor itself, `ManuallyDrop::drop(slot)` leaves the contained value's memory unchanged, retaining a bit-pattern valid for `T` as far as the compiler is concerned.

name: unsafe fn drop (slot : & mut ManuallyDrop < T >)
rule: Unless the contained value is a packed struct, `ManuallyDrop::drop(slot)` calls its destructor in place without moving the value.

name: unsafe fn drop (slot : & mut ManuallyDrop < T >)
rule: `ManuallyDrop::drop(slot)` may safely be used to drop pinned data when `T` is not `repr(packed)`.

name: const unsafe fn assume_init (self) -> T
rule: Before calling `MaybeUninit<T>::assume_init`, the caller must ensure that `self` contains a fully initialized `T`; calling it on content that is not fully initialized causes immediate undefined behavior.

name: const unsafe fn assume_init (self) -> T
rule: Before performing safe operations on the `T` returned by `MaybeUninit<T>::assume_init`, including dropping it, any additional invariants required by those operations must hold; merely satisfying type-level initialization requirements does not ensure those operations are safe.

name: const unsafe fn assume_init_read (& self) -> T
rule: The caller must ensure that the contents of `self` are fully initialized as a valid `T` before calling `assume_init_read`; calling it on contents that are not fully initialized causes undefined behavior.

name: const unsafe fn assume_init_read (& self) -> T
rule: When using multiple copies of the contents of `self`, whether by calling `assume_init_read` multiple times or by calling `assume_init_read` and then `assume_init`, the caller must ensure that the data may safely be duplicated; `assume_init_read` makes a bitwise copy even when `T` does not implement `Copy`.

name: unsafe fn assume_init_drop (& mut self)
rule: Before calling `MaybeUninit<T>::assume_init_drop`, the caller must ensure that the contained value is fully initialized.

name: unsafe fn assume_init_drop (& mut self)
rule: Before calling `MaybeUninit<T>::assume_init_drop`, the caller must ensure that all additional invariants of `T` are satisfied, including those relied on by the `Drop` implementation of `T` or its members.

name: const unsafe fn assume_init_ref (& self) -> & T
rule: The caller must ensure that the value contained in `self` is fully initialized as a valid `T` before calling `assume_init_ref`; calling it on content that is not yet fully initialized causes undefined behavior.

name: const unsafe fn assume_init_mut (& mut self) -> & mut T
rule: Before calling `MaybeUninit<T>::assume_init_mut`, the caller must ensure that the contained `T` is fully initialized; calling it on uninitialized or partially initialized contents is undefined behavior, so it must not be used to initialize the value.

name: const unsafe fn array_assume_init < const N : usize > (array : [Self ; N]) -> [T ; N]
rule: The caller must ensure that every element of `array` is in an initialized state before calling `MaybeUninit::<T>::array_assume_init`.

name: const unsafe fn slice_assume_init_ref (slice : & [Self]) -> & [T]
rule: For safety, every element of `slice` must contain a fully initialized value of type `T` before calling `slice_assume_init_ref`.

name: const unsafe fn slice_assume_init_mut (slice : & mut [Self]) -> & mut [T]
rule: The caller must ensure that every `MaybeUninit<T>` element in `slice` is fully initialized before calling `slice_assume_init_mut`; calling it with any element not fully initialized causes undefined behavior.

name: unsafe fn assume_init_drop (& mut self)
rule: Before calling `assume_init_drop`, every `MaybeUninit<T>` in the slice must be fully initialized; calling it with any content not fully initialized causes undefined behavior.

name: unsafe fn assume_init_drop (& mut self)
rule: Before calling `assume_init_drop`, every contained value must satisfy all additional invariants of `T`, including those relied on by the `Drop` implementation of `T` or its members.

name: const unsafe fn assume_init_ref (& self) -> & [T]
rule: To call `assume_init_ref` safely, every `MaybeUninit<T>` in `self` must contain a fully initialized `T`; calling it when any element is not fully initialized causes undefined behavior.

name: const unsafe fn assume_init_mut (& mut self) -> & mut [T]
rule: Before calling `assume_init_mut`, the caller must ensure that every `MaybeUninit<T>` in `self` is fully initialized; calling it with any uninitialized element causes undefined behavior. In particular, `assume_init_mut` cannot be used to initialize a `MaybeUninit` slice.

name: const unsafe fn transmute < Src , Dst > (src : Src) -> Dst
rule: The argument passed to `transmute::<Src, Dst>` must be valid at type `Src`.

name: const unsafe fn transmute < Src , Dst > (src : Src) -> Dst
rule: The result of `transmute::<Src, Dst>` must be valid at type `Dst`.

name: const unsafe fn transmute < Src , Dst > (src : Src) -> Dst
rule: The caller need not ensure alignment of the transmuted values themselves: because `transmute` passes values by value, the compiler ensures that both `Src` and `Dst` are properly aligned.

name: const unsafe fn transmute < Src , Dst > (src : Src) -> Dst
rule: When transmuting values that point elsewhere, such as pointers, references, or boxes, the caller must ensure proper alignment of the pointed-to values.

name: const unsafe fn transmute < Src , Dst > (src : Src) -> Dst
rule: In a `const` context, transmuting a pointer to an integer is undefined behavior unless the pointer was originally created from an integer, including through `transmute`, an integer-to-pointer cast, a helper such as `dangling`, or a semantically equivalent conversion such as punning through `repr(C)` union fields. This restriction also applies when the integer is nested inside an array, tuple, struct, or enum; `MaybeUninit<usize>` is not considered an integer type for this restriction.

name: const unsafe fn transmute < Src , Dst > (src : Src) -> Dst
rule: A pointer constructed by transmuting an integer to a pointer must not be used for non-zero-sized memory accesses; such accesses are currently considered undefined behavior. This also applies when the integer is nested inside an array, tuple, struct, or enum.

name: const unsafe fn transmute < Src , Dst > (src : Src) -> Dst
rule: Transmuting `*const ()` to `MaybeUninit<usize>` is permitted; `MaybeUninit<usize>` is not considered an integer type for the pointer-to-integer transmutation restrictions.

name: const unsafe fn transmute < Src , Dst > (src : Src) -> Dst
rule: Calling `assume_init()` on the result of transmuting `*const ()` to `MaybeUninit<usize>` completes the pointer-to-integer transmutation; in a `const` context, this is undefined behavior unless the original pointer was created from an integer.

name: const unsafe fn transmute < Src , Dst > (src : Src) -> Dst
rule: When using `transmute` to change the inner type of a container's contents, the caller must preserve all of the container's invariants, including any requirements involving element size, alignment, or `TypeId`.

name: const unsafe fn transmute < Src , Dst > (src : Src) -> Dst
rule: When using `transmute` to change the element type of a `Vec`, the source and destination element types must have equal sizes.

name: const unsafe fn transmute < Src , Dst > (src : Src) -> Dst
rule: When using `transmute` to change the element type of a `Vec`, the source and destination element types must have equal alignments.

name: const unsafe fn size_of_val_raw < T : ? Sized > (val : * const T) -> usize
rule: If T is Sized, size_of_val_raw(val) is always safe to call.

name: const unsafe fn size_of_val_raw < T : ? Sized > (val : * const T) -> usize
rule: If the unsized tail of T is a slice and its dynamic tail length is not 0, calling size_of_val_raw(val) requires the slice tail's length to be an initialized integer.

name: const unsafe fn size_of_val_raw < T : ? Sized > (val : * const T) -> usize
rule: If the unsized tail of T is a slice and its dynamic tail length is not 0, calling size_of_val_raw(val) requires the size of the entire value, including the dynamic tail and statically sized prefix, in bytes to fit in isize.

name: const unsafe fn size_of_val_raw < T : ? Sized > (val : * const T) -> usize
rule: If the unsized tail of T is a slice with dynamic tail length 0, size_of_val_raw(val) is safe to call.

name: const unsafe fn size_of_val_raw < T : ? Sized > (val : * const T) -> usize
rule: If the unsized tail of T is a trait object, calling size_of_val_raw(val) requires the vtable part of val to point to a valid vtable acquired by an unsizing coercion.

name: const unsafe fn size_of_val_raw < T : ? Sized > (val : * const T) -> usize
rule: If the unsized tail of T is a trait object, calling size_of_val_raw(val) requires the size of the entire value, including the dynamic tail and statically sized prefix, in bytes to fit in isize.

name: const unsafe fn size_of_val_raw < T : ? Sized > (val : * const T) -> usize
rule: If the unsized tail of T is an extern type, size_of_val_raw(val) is always safe to call, even though it may panic or return the wrong value.

name: const unsafe fn size_of_val_raw < T : ? Sized > (val : * const T) -> usize
rule: If T is not Sized and its unsized tail is neither a slice, a trait object, nor an extern type, calling size_of_val_raw(val) is not allowed for safety.

name: const unsafe fn align_of_val_raw < T : ? Sized > (val : * const T) -> usize
rule: Every reference to a value of type T must have an address that is a multiple of the alignment in bytes returned by align_of_val_raw(val).

name: const unsafe fn align_of_val_raw < T : ? Sized > (val : * const T) -> usize
rule: If T is Sized, align_of_val_raw(val) is always safe to call.

name: const unsafe fn align_of_val_raw < T : ? Sized > (val : * const T) -> usize
rule: If T has a slice unsized tail with nonzero dynamic length, calling align_of_val_raw(val) requires the slice-tail length in val to be an initialized integer.

name: const unsafe fn align_of_val_raw < T : ? Sized > (val : * const T) -> usize
rule: If T has a slice unsized tail with nonzero dynamic length, calling align_of_val_raw(val) requires the size of the entire value, including the dynamic tail and statically sized prefix, to fit in isize.

name: const unsafe fn align_of_val_raw < T : ? Sized > (val : * const T) -> usize
rule: If T has a slice unsized tail whose dynamic length is 0, align_of_val_raw(val) is safe to call.

name: const unsafe fn align_of_val_raw < T : ? Sized > (val : * const T) -> usize
rule: If T has a trait-object unsized tail, calling align_of_val_raw(val) requires the vtable part of val to point to a valid vtable acquired by an unsizing coercion.

name: const unsafe fn align_of_val_raw < T : ? Sized > (val : * const T) -> usize
rule: If T has a trait-object unsized tail, calling align_of_val_raw(val) requires the size of the entire value, including the dynamic tail and statically sized prefix, to fit in isize.

name: const unsafe fn align_of_val_raw < T : ? Sized > (val : * const T) -> usize
rule: If T has an extern-type unsized tail, align_of_val_raw(val) is always safe to call, even though it may panic or return the wrong value.

name: const unsafe fn align_of_val_raw < T : ? Sized > (val : * const T) -> usize
rule: If T is unsized and its unsized tail is neither a slice, a trait object, nor an extern type, calling align_of_val_raw(val) is not allowed for safety.

name: const unsafe fn zeroed < T > () -> T
rule: Calling `zeroed::<T>()` is safe only if the all-zero byte-pattern represents a valid value of `T`; reference types (`&U`, `&mut U`) and function-pointer types do not satisfy this requirement, and calling `zeroed` for them causes immediate undefined behavior.

name: unsafe fn uninitialized < T > () -> T
rule: Calling `uninitialized::<T>()` requires that the uninitialized memory produced satisfies `T`'s initialization invariant. Calling it for nearly all types, including integer types and arrays of integer types, causes immediate undefined behavior even if the result is unused.

name: const unsafe fn transmute_copy < Src , Dst > (src : & Src) -> Dst
rule: For safety, `src` must be valid for `size_of::<Dst>()` bytes.

name: const unsafe fn transmute_copy < Src , Dst > (src : & Src) -> Dst
rule: For safety, `size_of::<Dst>()` must not exceed `size_of::<Src>()`; a larger `Dst` causes undefined behavior.

name: const unsafe fn transmute_copy < Src , Dst > (src : & Src) -> Dst
rule: `Dst` may have stricter alignment requirements than `Src` without making the call unsafe on that account.

name: trait TransmuteFrom <Src , const ASSUME : Assume = { Assume :: NOTHING }> where Src : ? Sized ,
rule: If `Self: TransmuteFrom<Src, ASSUME>` and the programmer guarantees that the safety assumptions specified by `ASSUME` are satisfied, the compiler guarantees that the bits of a value of type `Src` can be soundly union-transmuted into `Self`, including conversions that extend the bits of `Src` with trailing padding to fill trailing uninitialized bytes of `Self`.

name: unsafe fn transmute (src : Src) -> Self where Src : Sized , Self : Sized ,
rule: If ASSUME.alignment is true, the caller must guarantee that the addresses of references in the returned Self satisfy the alignment requirements of their referent types.

name: unsafe fn transmute (src : Src) -> Self where Src : Sized , Self : Sized ,
rule: If ASSUME.lifetimes is true, the caller must guarantee that references in the returned Self will not outlive their referents.

name: unsafe fn transmute (src : Src) -> Self where Src : Sized , Self : Sized ,
rule: If ASSUME.safety is true, the returned value might not satisfy the library safety invariants of Self, and the caller must guarantee that undefined behavior does not arise from uses of the returned value.

name: unsafe fn transmute (src : Src) -> Self where Src : Sized , Self : Sized ,
rule: If ASSUME.validity is true, the caller must guarantee that src is a bit-valid instance of Self.

name: unsafe fn transmute (src : Src) -> Self where Src : Sized , Self : Sized ,
rule: When satisfying any caller safety obligations selected by ASSUME, the caller must not assume that TransmuteFrom inherently guarantees layout portability across toolchains, targets, or compilations.

name: unsafe fn transmute (src : Src) -> Self where Src : Sized , Self : Sized ,
rule: When satisfying any caller safety obligations selected by ASSUME, the caller must not assume that TransmuteFrom inherently guarantees layout SemVer stability across versions of the crates defining Src and Self.
